unverified: All 83 claims are found; nothing failed the check. The items below were read but not recorded as claims, or are inferences.

Release years 1928-1932 for Hirai Hideko and 1929 for Satō Chiyako come from Wikipedia's dated list of their Victor records; that the Victor compilation tracks on iTunes are those same records is an inference (Hirai stopped singing dōyō in 1934 and the reissues are Victor's own).

The first dōyō record (Kanariya by members of the Akai Tori girls' singing society, Nipponophone, June 1920) is on the ja Wikipedia infobox for かなりや; no playable or catalogued copy was found, so it is not in the playlist.
No recording by Motoori Midori, 'Japan's first dōyō singer', was found on iTunes or MusicBrainz; she is named only as a marker.

ended is null: ja Wikipedia says the narrow 'literary dōyō' came to an end around 1973 (end of the Record Award's dōyō prize), but new dōyō are still written and presented by the Japan Dōyō Association. The 1973 claim was dropped to keep the claim count down.
ja Wikipedia's 童謡 and 川田正子 articles carry a 'sources needed' banner; the facts used from them are standard but the articles are under-sourced.
Peak window 1919-1955 is a judgement from dated facts (magazine golden age of the 1920s, postwar boom, 1954 sales remark), not stated by any source.
